sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: The service experiment qualifies as persistent skill evolution, but the detailed web examples above cannot be assumed to be its retained service policies.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: τ³-Bench. HarnessX dialogue and tool-use configuration.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: The reported service runs ship prompt rules and processors addressing policy ordering and premature actions. No tool edits are shipped in these runs.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: This is a distinct experiment from WebShop, not an additional paper. Repeated search-pool evaluation and separate co-training experiments must remain distinct from frozen-model generalization.

sources.name: HarnessX
sources.locator: Experimental setup; Appendix Additional Results, τ³-Bench

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: Harvey LAB; transfer to JobBench, GDPval and APEX-Agents. A study-specific ReAct loop over an MCP gateway with a dynamic toolbelt and ReSum-style context management.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Regularized edits optimize the workspace harness on Harvey LAB, and the resulting harness is evaluated on a pristine in-domain split and three unseen professional-work suites.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: The paper's detailed accepted-edit table contains coding and engineering examples, not a Harvey-specific diff. We record workspace evolution and transfer without importing those other domains' mechanisms.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: TextArena. A fixed LLM-action/retry scaffold with function interfaces for synthesizing action proposals and legality checks. The LLM without this harness is a comparison baseline.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Environment feedback fills and refines the supplied propose_action and is_legal_action interfaces. In the verifier configuration, the existing loop checks LLM-proposed moves and returns an illegal-action warning before retrying. Appendix D.2 exposes chess coordinate parsing, king location and attack detection; a separate configuration synthesizes whole Python policies.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: We count the verifier configuration as a harness around an LLM. Pure code policies replace task-time LLM execution and are a distinct boundary case; neither changes the outer search rule.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: Pokémon Red and Emerald. A minimal screenshot/map/button interface with no curated skills or subagents.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: An automated Refiner revises prompts, subagents, executable skills and memory during a continuous run, using navigation loops and tool failures as feedback.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: This record concerns the automated configuration. Historical Gemini Plays Pokémon milestones involve human refinement; detailed historical battle-agent changes cannot be attributed to the automated experiment. Model co-training is separate.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: Liar's Dice; Balatro; Slay the Spire 2. Game-specific base harnesses with fixed environment interfaces.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Selected Liar's Dice self-rollout harnesses parse game state, calculate claim probabilities and legal raises, and compare calling with raising. Appendix B gives simplified sketches of selected harnesses. Its OneCall-Wild1 variant uses a Bayesian escalation model; during deep same-face escalation, with at least two own contributions, it overrides raising when calling's expected value is higher by a margin. On Balatro and Slay the Spire 2, successful demonstrations supply a separate source of evidence for persistent harness revision.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Appendix G audits a selected Meta-Harness baseline whose proposed Balatro hook never reached the model. That inactive hook is negative evidence, not a successful DemoEvolve discovery; held-out game seeds are evaluated separately.

sources.name: DemoEvolve
sources.locator: Sections 4.1–4.3; Appendices B, C and G

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: Minecraft 50-task curriculum. Static task interface and capability library around a frozen model.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Experience supports capability and workflow revisions; retained skill tests gate later updates, extending reuse across crafting and dependent operations.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: This is one sequential Minecraft experiment. It documents retention-based capability evolution, without establishing that its updater itself evolves or exposing every final skill diff.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: LIBERO-Pro; RoboCasa. Frozen VLA policy with an initially unevolved critic/recovery harness.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: The stove-placement lineage adds object-relative pregrasp. After grasp failure it releases and restages, chooses a proposal different from remembered failed grasps, and checks stability within a retry budget. Placement lowers the object until support is detected, then releases and retreats until separation is confirmed.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Code critics propose interventions; the fixed orchestrator authorizes them and the official task predicate determines success. Section 4.3 applies the cumulative stove-task checkpoints to PnP-Sink, PnP-Cabinet and PnP-Toaster without further evolution: mean success rises from 64% to 84%. This supports reuse of the complete recovery stack, not each branch independently. Historical regression and held-out checks gate reusable updates.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: VLABench. Generic planner guidance and a context builder accumulating all prior rounds.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: The evolved skill emits actor-compatible primitive commands with exact entity names. The final context builder emphasizes current images and recent execution state, compresses older rounds and exposes stagnation.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: VLA weights and low-level action generation remain fixed. The before/after artifacts support actor-aware command and context changes; ESI-Bench active-perception changes are a separate setting.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: LIBERO/Pro; RoboCasa; other embodied suites. Code-as-policy interface around fixed action primitives.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Execution failures revise programs and become node-local skills. The retained align-object-to-basket-mouth skill diagnoses a 5.3 cm depth error caused by estimating the target from all basket-mask points. It changes basket_center_world to use medians of upper-rim points for both horizontal position and height, with an all-points fallback when fewer than five rim points remain. The existing placement servo is unchanged.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: The program stays fixed within each rollout and evolves between rollouts. Post-training on collected expert trajectories is a separate weight-update experiment; the published skill is not an isolated causal ablation.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: SimplerEnv Bridge uses frozen GR00T; three real-world tasks use a frozen fine-tuned π₀.₅ policy. A light agent has an observation/intervention interface, and playbook refinement starts from teacher guidance distilled from initial development rollouts; no-playbook agents are comparison baselines.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Strong-agent experience and recipient feedback revise a reusable intervention playbook: re-identify occluded objects, distinguish weak from empty grasps, inspect action mismatches, and verify support before release.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: The text guides interventions through the existing policy. On the same 48 held-out Bridge instances, Luna succeeds at 43.8% without a playbook, 31.3% with the initial teacher-distilled playbook and 66.7% with the refined playbook. A Luna-derived refined playbook instead reaches 22.9%; stronger-teacher guidance is not interchangeable with self-refinement. These whole-playbook comparisons do not isolate individual rules or show that the distillation algorithm rewrites itself.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: LVBench evolution; frozen evaluation on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, EgoSchema and MLVU. The seed already has global/local inspection, transcript/OCR access and observation memory.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Retained revisions add frame-linked findings with uncertainty, relations over existing observations, selective 64-frame overviews and occurrence counting. Graph queries process no new frames; counting consolidates overlapping detections.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: The full harness uses fewer frames and answers more accurately than the seed on the four reported suites. Table 2 ablates editor investigation and selection gates, not individual deployed tools. Frame savings exclude editor cost and are not total-compute savings.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: LongVideoBench; Video-MME; Video-Holmes; transfer to Video-MMMU/MMVU. A task contract and video/transcript/VLM APIs for constructing executable video-agent programs; no separately named seed is established here.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: MCTS with multi-fidelity validation searches selective-observation programs; retained harnesses form budget-specialized choices in a mixture.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Search design and budget routing are specified by the method. The reviewed text documents evolution and validation trajectories more clearly than final per-tool diffs, so we do not invent a discovered frame-sampling rule.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: Charades-STA; ActivityNet; QVHighlights; ReXTime; TimeLens-Bench. The seed predicts one interval from 64 uniform frames and generic instructions.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Instructions check repeated occurrences and event boundaries. Coarse sampling or unusual interval length triggers another prediction; substantial disagreement triggers a third. Start and end times are separately combined by medians.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: All compared configurations use the same 64 frames; extra calls add computation. Figure 3 shows a recovered kettle interval. For the light switch, the instruction-only variant already moves the correct seed interval [0,1] to [1,3]; the three-call variant returns [1,4]. Extra calls therefore do not recover this instruction-level regression. These are cases; Table 3 separates code and instruction contributions across settings.

signals.scope: Figure 3 kettle example; the frozen record does not assign this example to one of its five benchmark memberships.
signals.summary: A recovered interval is reported for the kettle case, not a dataset-wide component effect.
signals.evidence_quote: Figure 3 shows a recovered kettle interval.

signals.scope: Figure 3 light-switch example only; not assigned to a specific benchmark in this annotation.
signals.summary: The instruction variant moves a correct interval to an incorrect one; extra calls do not recover it.
signals.evidence_quote: Extra calls therefore do not recover this instruction-level regression.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: COCO detection/captioning; RefCOCO; VQAv2. Frozen VLM with editable external task interfaces, memory, capabilities and router.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Sequential non-parametric updates balance learning the next visual task against preserving previously solved anchor examples.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Disabling memory updates mainly reduces captioning performance; fixing the router produces its largest task-level decline on VQAv2. Interface updates contribute most visibly to captioning and VQAv2. These ablations support different component roles, not a published final grounding-specific rule; variants follow different update trajectories. This is the same paper as the QA and Minecraft records.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: MultiBanana; OmniContext. Search starts from a one-call generator and GEMS.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: The selected lineage binds prompt elements to references, generates subject-led and background-led drafts, checks hard failures before order-swapped comparisons, and generates a third draft from reference-specific complaints. When hard-failure counts tie, the challenger replaces the incumbent only if it wins both presentation orders. This selector uses the target reasoning model; the search evaluator is separate.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Direct-edit variants leave the retained lineage. The fixed-three-image ablations replace removed drafts with another sample and replace failure-aware selection with Best-of-N. They support the combined selector rather than isolating order swapping. Harness-search cost is separate; generator weights stay fixed.

sources.name: AutoRef
sources.locator: Sections 4–5 and 6.5; Table 4; Appendices D and H.2

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: GenEval 2; DPG-Bench; OneIG splits. A ComfyUI graph-construction agent starts with predefined tools and four general image-generation skills. The supplied refinement architecture includes a visual verifier; the Base comparison executes once without verifier feedback.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Cross-run traces and feedback produce reusable SKILL.md procedures; reported examples include spatial/count binding, attribute binding and benchmark-dependent style or detail guidance.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Typed editing, invalid-edit rollback and the region verifier are supplied architecture. Skill-read counts establish consultation, not isolated causal quality. The reported workflow-edit distribution describes per-image actions; it does not by itself identify persistent edits to the harness.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: GenEval2; T2I-CompBench++; WISE. Frozen image generators wrapped by an initial multi-responsibility harness.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Figure 6 illustrates localized counting-policy, spatial-composition, attribute-binding tool-knowledge and action–object memory changes.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Earlier Appendix B examples phrased as possible patches illustrate the edit space, rather than establish exact retained diffs. Trace, No-Patch and held-out gates are supplied evolution machinery. Figure 6 gives qualitative cases; aggregate scores do not isolate each patch. The experiments adapt a separate harness for each generator, rather than transfer one unchanged harness across them.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: Long-video production categories and held-out cases. Fixed foundation skills plus initial category composition and creator skills.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Training feedback revises reusable composition skills and the instructions that create them; category-local creator skills are merged for unseen-category transfer.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Composition skills are frozen for held-out cases; the merged creator is frozen before receiving unseen-category skill queries and does not update on OOD execution feedback. Section 4.2 and Appendix C specify the update and merging procedures, but the reviewed text does not establish an exact final per-category instruction diff.

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: CineScope; AnimeShooter; ViStoryBench. CineForge-Produce starts with a fixed initial production policy and supplied production stages.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: Cross-story evidence produces bounded stage-local changes to a persistent textual production policy, admitted through fresh replay and, where needed, paired stochastic evaluation.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: The permitted patch types in Appendix B.3 are not a list of exact retained edits. Three-round checkpoint evaluation is read-only on a fixed unseen split. Review-workload measurement overrides editable operational-review settings with a frozen audit reviewer, so lower workload does not result from simply weakening that reviewer.
